title: Product slices are scoped `@product/…`
subject: main
summary: Scope every workspace package by its tier: `@configs/…` · `@libs/…` · `@modules/…` ([[seed slice|seed slices]]) · `@product/…` ([[product slice|product slices]]

adr.context: The decision `scope-names-the-tier` named the product-specific tier `@features/…`, after the `features/` folders product code once lived in. That folder no longer exists: product code lives in [[product slice|product slices]] under `apps/main/slices/product/<s>/`, so `@features/…` named a tier the repo doesn't have — and read as an invitation to recreate a `features/` folder.
adr.decision: Scope every workspace package by its tier: `@configs/…` · `@libs/…` · `@modules/…` ([[seed slice|seed slices]]) · `@product/…` ([[product slice|product slices]]) · `@apps/…`. A product slice's package is named after its folder: `apps/main/slices/product/song/` → `@product/song`.
consequences: Everything else in `scope-names-the-tier` still holds: violations read at the call site, boundary rules are scope-to-scope lint patterns, promoting a product slice to a seed slice rewrites its imports, and the registry constraint stands.
No product slice package exists yet, so nothing is renamed — the first one under `apps/main/slices/product/` takes the scope.
Seed slices keep `@modules/…`: the existing packages (`@modules/user-organization-mgmt`, `@modules/notifications`) don't move.
